reconcile.note: Matthew Henry judges Lot righteous by his overall course of life, not by isolated failures like the daughter-offering or the drunken incest of Genesis 19.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Was Lot righteous?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/lot_righteous.html) (2013).

sides.snippet: I have two virgin daughters. Please let me bring them out to you, and do you to them as is good in your eyes
sides.verseText: See now, I have two virgin daughters. Please let me bring them out to you, and do you to them as is good in your eyes. Only don't do anything to these men, because they have come under the shadow of my roof.\"

sides.snippet: delivered righteous Lot, who was very distressed by the lustful life of the wicked
sides.verseText: and delivered righteous Lot, who was very distressed by the lustful life of the wicked
